findings.title: Silence drawer will never open when rulerRule is undefined (new list view)
findings.body: When `rule` (rulerRule) is undefined — which is the case in the new alert list view that no longer fetches ruler data — the condition `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` evaluates to false. This means even though `canSilence` can be true (via the prom rule abilities path in AlertRuleMenu) and the user can click 'Silence notifications' in the dropdown menu, the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` will never render because `showSilenceDrawer` is gated behind the rulerRule type check. The user clicks the menu item and nothing happens.

findings.title: Pause menu item will never render when rulerRule is undefined despite canPause being true
findings.body: The `canPause` variable can now be true via the `grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed` path (when promRule is a Grafana rule and rulerRule is undefined). However, the render condition on line 123 additionally requires `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)`, which returns false when `rulerRule` is undefined. This means in the new list view (where ruler is not fetched), the Pause button will never appear even though the ability system says the user can pause the rule. The `MenuItemPauseRule` component also requires a `rulerRule` prop, so a deeper refactor is needed to support pause without ruler data.

findings.title: Delete menu item will never render when rulerRule is undefined despite canDelete being true
findings.body: Similar to the Pause issue: `canDelete` can be true via the grafana prom rule abilities path, but the render condition `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}` requires `rulerRule` to be truthy. In the new list view where ruler data is not fetched, `rulerRule` is undefined, so the Delete menu item will never appear. Additionally, `handleDelete` is called with `rulerRule` as an argument (line 172), so the delete flow itself depends on having a ruler rule object.

findings.title: Federated rule check removed from useAllRulerRuleAbilities, allowing edit/delete of federated rules
findings.body: The old `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` checked `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` to determine if a rule was in a federated group (which should make it immutable). The refactored `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` hardcodes `isFederated = false` with a TODO comment. Since `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (marked deprecated but still used via `useAlertRuleAbility`) now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, federated rules in Mimir/Cloud data sources will incorrectly appear as editable and deletable in the old list view and rule details view until the TODO is addressed.

findings.title: Inline actions array in useMemo dependency defeats memoization
findings.body: In `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (and `useRulerRuleAbilities`), the `actions` parameter is included in the `useMemo` dependency array. All call sites (e.g., AlertRuleMenu.tsx line 73-79) pass an inline array literal, which creates a new reference on every render. This causes the useMemo to recompute every render, negating the memoization benefit. Consider using a stable reference (e.g., a constant array or JSON-serialized key) or removing `actions` from deps and using a ref.

findings.title: Redundant type narrowing creates unnecessary undefined assignment
findings.body: Inside the `if (prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule))` block, the code does `const promAlertingRule = rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting ? rule : undefined`. The outer type guard already narrows `rule` to `GrafanaPromAlertingRuleDTO`, so this inner check is always true and `promAlertingRule` can never be undefined. While not a runtime bug, it makes the code misleading — a reader might think `promAlertingRule` could be undefined and that the subsequent `promAlertingRule?.state` and `promAlertingRule?.totals` optional chaining is necessary, when in fact `rule` itself could be used directly.
